quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Extra Shifts] Carmen has asked for the Saturday shift three weeks in a row. Last week she told a coworker that concert tickets go on sale in April and she wants "to be ready."
quests.question: Why is Carmen most likely working extra shifts?
options: She is hoping to be promoted this spring.
Her manager is making the whole team work weekends.
She dislikes spending her weekends at home.
She is saving money for something she wants to buy.
quests.correctAnswer: She is saving money for something she wants to buy.
quests.hint: Connect the extra work with the date she mentions.
quests.explanation: She keeps volunteering for extra hours, and she links April to tickets and being "ready." Together these clues suggest she is earning money for the tickets. Nothing says the shifts are compulsory.
clueWords: Saturday shift three weeks in a row

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Two Alarms] Dmitri sets two alarms, puts his phone on the far side of the room, and lays out his clothes before bed.
quests.question: What is tomorrow morning likely to be like for Dmitri?
options: He has to be up early and does not want to oversleep.
He has just bought a new phone.
He is planning to work late tonight and needs to remember his phone charger.
He plans to stay in bed until noon.
quests.correctAnswer: He has to be up early and does not want to oversleep.
quests.hint: Ask why someone would make it hard to reach the alarm.
quests.explanation: Two alarms and a phone he must walk across the room to reach show he wants to be sure to wake up. Laying out clothes suggests he will leave in a hurry.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Fridge Note] Mr. Tanaka leaves a note on the office fridge: "To whoever took my lunch, I don't mind about the food. Please just leave the container. It was my daughter's."
quests.question: Why does Mr. Tanaka ask for the container back?
options: It belongs to the company.
It has personal value to him.
He thinks he knows which coworker took it.
He wants the food replaced.
quests.correctAnswer: It has personal value to him.
quests.hint: Notice what he says he does not mind, and what he asks for instead.
quests.explanation: He says the food does not matter, then asks for the container and says whose it was. This shows the container matters for personal reasons.
clueWords: I don't mind about the food

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Eight Ten] The train leaves at 8:10. Anil's taxi is stuck behind a truck on the ring road, and the clock on the dashboard says 8:02.
quests.question: What will probably happen?
options: The train will wait for him.
He will decide to walk the rest of the way.
He will arrive with time to spare.
He may miss his train.
quests.correctAnswer: He may miss his train.
quests.hint: Compare the time left with how far the taxi has to go.
quests.explanation: Only eight minutes remain and the taxi is not moving. That makes missing the train a real possibility, and nothing suggests the train will wait.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Weekend Away] While cleaning, Ola unplugs the freezer to reach the socket and forgets to plug it back in. That evening she leaves for a weekend trip.
quests.question: What is most likely to be true when she gets home?
options: The food in the freezer will have started to thaw.
The socket will have been repaired.
The freezer will be colder than before.
The food will be fresher than before.
quests.correctAnswer: The food in the freezer will have started to thaw.
quests.hint: Think about what a freezer needs in order to stay cold.
quests.explanation: A freezer stays cold only when it has power. Left unplugged for a weekend, it will warm up and the food will begin to thaw.
clueWords: forgets to plug it back in

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Late Project] Ms. Ruiz tells the class that any project handed in after Friday loses ten points. Kabir submits his on Monday morning.
quests.question: What can you conclude about Kabir's mark?
options: It will be higher because he had extra time.
It will not be affected by the date.
It will probably be lower because of the delay.
He will have to redo the whole project.
quests.correctAnswer: It will probably be lower because of the delay.
quests.hint: What rule did the teacher announce, and when did Kabir submit?
quests.explanation: The rule attaches a penalty to work handed in after Friday. Monday is after Friday, so his mark will probably lose points.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Interesting Hat] "That's an interesting hat," Uncle Femi says, turning it over slowly. He smiles politely and puts it back on the shelf.
quests.question: What does Uncle Femi probably think of the hat?
options: He loves it and wants to buy it.
He wants to wear it right away.
He thinks it is very cheap.
He is not very impressed by it.
quests.correctAnswer: He is not very impressed by it.
quests.hint: Compare his words with what he does with the hat.
quests.explanation: "Interesting" can be a polite word for something you do not admire. He smiles politely and returns the hat to the shelf, which shows he is not interested in it.
clueWords: puts it back on the shelf

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Small Voice] "I'm fine, really," Amara says, her voice small. "You should go out with your friends tonight." After he leaves, she turns off the TV and looks at the empty sofa.
quests.question: What is Amara probably feeling?
options: Tired of having company.
Lonely, although she has not said so.
Cheerful and relaxed.
Angry at her friends.
quests.correctAnswer: Lonely, although she has not said so.
quests.hint: Compare her words with her voice and with what she does afterwards.
quests.explanation: Her words say she is fine, but her small voice and the way she looks at the empty sofa say something different. The likely feeling is loneliness.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [In the Back] "Do you have this in a bigger size?" the customer asks. The assistant checks the shelf, then says, "Let me look in the back."
quests.question: What does the assistant's answer suggest?
options: The shop never sells that size.
The size is not on display, but it may be in storage.
The item is sold out in every store.
The assistant is unsure whether the shop stocks that item at all this season.
quests.correctAnswer: The size is not on display, but it may be in storage.
quests.hint: She did not say yes or no. What did she decide to do?
quests.explanation: She checks the shelf first and then goes to look in the back. That suggests the size is not out but she thinks it might be stored there.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Quiet Lately] Luca used to answer every question in class. Since the school trip, he stares at his desk and hardly says a word.
quests.question: What might explain the change in Luca?
options: He wants to move to another school.
He has started to find the lessons too easy and is bored by them.
Something has upset or troubled him recently.
He has become more confident.
quests.correctAnswer: Something has upset or troubled him recently.
quests.hint: Compare how he behaved before the trip with how he behaves now.
quests.explanation: The passage sets "used to" against "since the trip," so the change began then. Staring down and staying silent suggest something is bothering him.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [New Haircut] Everyone at the office told Rita her new haircut looked great. All morning she kept touching it and frowning at her reflection in the window.
quests.question: How does Rita feel about her haircut?
options: She is not sure she likes it.
She did not hear the compliments.
She is annoyed at her coworkers.
She is thrilled with it.
quests.correctAnswer: She is not sure she likes it.
quests.hint: Compare what other people say with what Rita does.
quests.explanation: The compliments are positive, but Rita's frowning and constant touching show doubt. Her own reaction matters more here than what others say.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Flight Checks] Before the holidays, Sven checked flight prices every hour. Now he has not opened the website for two days, and a suitcase is open on his bed.
quests.question: What does the change in Sven's behaviour suggest?
options: He cannot afford the trip.
The website has stopped working.
He has lost interest in travelling.
He has already booked his flight.
quests.correctAnswer: He has already booked his flight.
quests.hint: What replaced the constant checking?
quests.explanation: The checking stopped and packing began. That sequence suggests he no longer needs to search because the decision has been made.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [After Lunch] The cafeteria is almost empty. Two workers are wiping tables and stacking chairs, and someone is switching off the lights at the far end.
quests.question: What stage of the lunch period does this scene suggest?
options: Early in the morning, before breakfast.
During a school assembly.
In the middle of the lunch rush.
Near the end of the lunch period.
quests.correctAnswer: Near the end of the lunch period.
quests.hint: Ask what workers do when a room is finished being used.
quests.explanation: Few people, stacked chairs, and lights going off show that the room is closing down after use, not opening up or in full use.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Three Photos] In the first photo, Dev wears a school uniform. In the second, he holds a diploma. In the third, he stands in a laboratory, wearing a white coat.
quests.question: Where does Dev's story seem to be heading?
options: He left school without finishing and later found a job as an assistant in a lab.
He dislikes science.
He finished school and went on to work or study in science.
He failed his final exams.
quests.correctAnswer: He finished school and went on to work or study in science.
quests.hint: Read the photos as a sequence, not one at a time.
quests.explanation: The order runs from school to a diploma to a laboratory. This progression suggests he has moved from school to science work or study.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Footprints] Muddy footprints lead from the back door across the kitchen floor. The kettle is still warm, and the back door is standing open.
quests.question: What do the footprints and the warm kettle suggest?
options: Someone has just cleaned the floor.
The kettle is broken.
The house has been empty for days.
Someone has come in very recently.
quests.correctAnswer: Someone has come in very recently.
quests.hint: What does a warm kettle tell you about time?
quests.explanation: Wet mud and a warm kettle both fade quickly, and the open door shows how someone came in. These clues point to a recent visitor.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Lost Wallet] Yara finds a wallet with two hundred dollars inside. She walks straight to the security desk and hands it to the guard, along with a note saying where she found it.
quests.question: What kind of person is Yara?
options: Nervous around officials.
Honest and thoughtful.
Careless with money.
Curious about strangers.
quests.correctAnswer: Honest and thoughtful.
quests.hint: Focus on what she does with the money and why she adds a note.
quests.explanation: She returns the wallet with the cash inside and adds a note to help the owner. These actions show honesty and care for others.
clueWords: walks straight to the security desk
a note saying where she found it

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Group Argument] While the others argue about who should do what, Hasan quietly writes each task on the board, adds names, and asks if anyone objects.
quests.question: How does Hasan deal with the argument?
options: He does not care about the project.
He wants to take the lead in the group and decide the tasks himself.
He prefers practical solutions to arguments.
He is afraid of speaking in public.
quests.correctAnswer: He prefers practical solutions to arguments.
quests.hint: What does his last question show about his approach?
quests.explanation: He writes tasks down and asks if anyone objects, which shows he wants a clear plan that people accept. That is problem-solving rather than taking control.
clueWords: writes each task on the board

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Extra Pens] Petra lends the new girl a pen because her pencil case is empty. The next day she brings a handful of spares "in case anyone else needs one."
quests.question: What kind of person does Petra seem to be?
options: She buys too many pens.
She is worried about running out of pens.
She is trying to make friends to get help with homework.
She notices what others need and tries to help.
quests.correctAnswer: She notices what others need and tries to help.
quests.hint: What did she do the next day, and why did she say she did it?
quests.explanation: She helped once, then prepared to help again. Her words, "in case anyone else needs one," show she is thinking about others.
clueWords: lends the new girl a pen
in case anyone else needs one

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Table Six] The people at table six have been checking their watches for forty minutes. The waiter walks past them twice without stopping and avoids their eyes.
quests.question: What is probably the problem?
options: The waiter is new and afraid of the customers.
They cannot pay the bill.
Their food is very late.
They ordered too much food.
quests.correctAnswer: Their food is very late.
quests.hint: Look at both what the customers do and what the waiter avoids.
quests.explanation: The customers are waiting and checking the time. The waiter avoids them, as if he has nothing good to say. This suggests a long delay with their order.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Back Row] The speaker keeps asking, "Can you all hear me?" In the back row, people lean forward and someone shakes their head.
quests.question: What is most likely wrong?
options: The sound is not reaching the back of the room.
The people at the back arrived late.
The speaker is talking about the wrong topic.
The room is too warm.
quests.correctAnswer: The sound is not reaching the back of the room.
quests.hint: Which action shows how the audience responds to the speaker's question?
quests.explanation: The question, the leaning forward, and the head shake all point to a hearing problem at the back of the room.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Old Container] Jelena opens the fridge, wrinkles her nose, and starts checking the dates on the containers.
quests.question: What is she most likely trying to do?
options: Check that the fridge is cold enough.
Find out what has gone bad.
Count how much food she has.
Decide what to cook for dinner.
quests.correctAnswer: Find out what has gone bad.
quests.hint: Notice her face before she looks at the dates.
quests.explanation: Wrinkling her nose suggests a smell she does not like. Checking dates then shows she is searching for something that may be spoiled.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Two Roads] Tariq can take the highway, which takes twenty minutes, or the coast road, which takes forty. On weekends he always takes the coast road.
quests.question: Why might Tariq choose the coast road at weekends?
options: He cares more about the drive than about speed.
He is usually running late.
He does not know the highway.
He picks up a friend on the coast.
quests.correctAnswer: He cares more about the drive than about speed.
quests.hint: What does he give up by choosing the coast road?
quests.explanation: He accepts twenty extra minutes each time. That suggests he values something about the drive itself, such as the scenery.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Two Classrooms] In Mr. Bell's class, students tiptoe in and whisper. In Ms. Dara's class, students chat and laugh until the bell, then start work at once.
quests.question: How do the two classes compare?
options: Mr. Bell is a new teacher.
Students dislike Ms. Dara's class.
Mr. Bell's class is stricter, but Ms. Dara's students still work well.
Mr. Bell's students are more talented than Ms. Dara's, so they behave more carefully.
quests.correctAnswer: Mr. Bell's class is stricter, but Ms. Dara's students still work well.
quests.hint: Look at how each group behaves before the bell and after it.
quests.explanation: Whispering suggests strict rules in Mr. Bell's room. In Ms. Dara's room the students relax, yet they start work as soon as the bell goes, so the class is not disorderly.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [The Old Phone] Grandpa Isaac took the new phone back to the shop and asked for his old one, the one with the big buttons.
quests.question: Why did he most likely return the new phone?
options: The old one was easier for him to use.
He wanted a phone with a better camera.
The new one was the wrong colour.
The new one was too expensive.
quests.correctAnswer: The old one was easier for him to use.
quests.hint: What feature of the old phone does the passage mention?
quests.explanation: He chose the old phone specifically because of its big buttons, which suggests the new one was harder to use.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Pool Times] NOTICE: The lap pool is closed from 12:00 to 2:00 every weekday for children's swimming lessons. Adults may use the family pool during this time.
quests.question: What can an adult swimmer infer?
options: Children are not allowed in the family pool.
They can still swim at midday, but in a different pool.
They cannot swim on weekdays.
The family pool is closed for lessons.
quests.correctAnswer: They can still swim at midday, but in a different pool.
quests.hint: Read who may use which pool at midday.
quests.explanation: The lap pool is closed for lessons, but the notice says adults may use the family pool. So adults can still swim, in another place.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Harbor Street] Attention passengers: because of road work, the 42 bus will not stop at Harbor Street today. Please get off at Market Square and walk five minutes.
quests.question: What does this mean for a passenger going to Harbor Street?
options: They can no longer reach that area today.
They will need to get off earlier and walk.
The bus will take a longer route to get there.
They must wait for a different bus.
quests.correctAnswer: They will need to get off earlier and walk.
quests.hint: Which stop should passengers use instead?
quests.explanation: The bus skips Harbor Street, but passengers are told to get off at Market Square and walk. So they can still reach it with a short walk.
clueWords: will not stop at Harbor Street

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Coach's Text] Coach: "Practice moved to 6:30 tonight. Bring water and your indoor shoes."
quests.question: Where will tonight's practice most likely be held?
options: It will take place indoors.
It will start earlier than usual.
It will be on the field as usual.
It has been cancelled.
quests.correctAnswer: It will take place indoors.
quests.hint: Which item on the list gives you information about the place?
quests.explanation: "Indoor shoes" tells the players where they will play. A change of time does not mean cancellation, and the practice is moved, not cancelled.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Broken Oven] The bakery's oven broke this morning. By noon the shelves were half empty, and the owner was writing "Sorry, fewer pastries today" on the board.
quests.question: Why were there fewer pastries?
options: The pastries were being kept for a party.
Customers had bought everything early.
Less could be baked because the oven was broken.
The owner decided to close early.
quests.correctAnswer: Less could be baked because the oven was broken.
quests.hint: Follow the order of events and how the owner explains it.
quests.explanation: The oven breaks in the morning, and by noon the shelves are half empty. The owner's apology on the board connects the shortage to a supply problem, not to unusual demand.

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [The Trophy] Everyone clapped when Malik's name was called. He walked up slowly, wiping his eyes, and held the trophy against his chest.
quests.question: How is Malik most likely feeling?
options: Sad about losing.
Embarrassed about being late.
Bored by the ceremony.
Moved and very happy.
quests.correctAnswer: Moved and very happy.
quests.hint: Think about why clapping and a trophy go together, then what tears might mean here.
quests.explanation: Applause and a trophy show he won. Walking slowly and holding the trophy close suggest deep emotion. The tears fit joy, not sadness.
clueWords: held the trophy against his chest

quests.instruction: Read the passage and select the correct inference.
quests.passage: [Table by the Window] The couple at the window table ordered coffee three times but left half their cake. They left a generous tip and told the waiter they would be back next week.
quests.question: How did the couple feel about their visit?
options: They disliked the food and will not return.
They enjoyed the café overall.
They were unhappy with the service.
They were in a hurry to leave.
quests.correctAnswer: They enjoyed the café overall.
quests.hint: Weigh the uneaten cake against the other two things they did.
quests.explanation: Half a cake left might suggest dislike, but they ordered more coffee, tipped well, and planned to return. Together these show they were pleased with the visit.
